warning.text:
Swimming is currently prohibited in the Neckar in Stuttgart!

Open-water swimming should only be practiced by experienced swimmers.

items.title: Forecast
items.text: The forecasting system analyzes various factors that affect water quality. Because we have only limited laboratory data available, the system can currently only predict “excellent” and “poor” categories based on the Bathing Water Regulation. It is trained to ensure that positive recommendations are as reliable as possible. Negative forecasts are accurate in only 50% of cases. The forecasts are intended to raise awareness and do not constitute official monitoring of water quality.

items.title: Pollution
items.text: After heavy rainfall, the river may contain microbiological contaminants. These are detected using the indicator bacteria E. coli and enterococci. The water remains contaminated for several days afterward. In addition, rivers may contain viruses, parasites, and chemical contaminants that are not included in the forecast. For healthy people, the risk of serious illness is low. However, people with pre-existing medical conditions should be especially cautious.

items.title: Federal Waterway
items.text: On federal waterways such as the Neckar, swimming is prohibited in shipping lanes and within 100 meters of structures such as weirs, locks, and bridges. Ships up to 105 meters long travel through these areas; they cannot swerve out of the way and create dangerous rip currents. Be sure to stay away from the center of the river and shipping structures.

items.title: Local Conditions
items.text: There are no designated swimming areas on the Neckar River. Anyone wishing to swim there should familiarise themselves with the local conditions und follow a few rules. Dangerous currents can form near bridges, structures and boats. Poor visibility makes it harder to spot hazards beneath the water's surface.
